questions.question: Which famous landmark is this?
questions.explanation: The Statue of Liberty was a present to the United States from France, unveiled in 1886.

questions.question: In which city is this famous building?
questions.explanation: The Sydney Opera House's roof is covered in more than a million tiles.

media.alt: A famous building by the water

questions.question: What is the official name of the London clock tower that holds the bell called Big Ben?
questions.explanation: It was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012 for the Queen's Diamond Jubilee; Big Ben is the great bell inside.

questions.question: In which country would you find the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
questions.explanation: The tower started to lean while it was still being built, more than 800 years ago.

questions.question: Which famous landmark is this?
questions.explanation: All the sections of the Great Wall added together stretch for more than 20,000 kilometres.

questions.question: This building, carved into a cliff, is in which ancient city?
questions.explanation: Petra, in Jordan, was carved straight into rose-red sandstone cliffs by the Nabataeans.

media.alt: A building carved into a rock face

questions.question: The Alhambra palace is in which Spanish city?
questions.explanation: Most of the Alhambra was built by the Nasrid rulers of Granada in the 13th and 14th centuries.

questions.question: Which Paris landmark was built as the entrance arch to the 1889 World's Fair?
questions.explanation: It was only meant to stand for 20 years.

questions.question: In which country is this temple?
questions.explanation: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world, and it appears on Cambodia's flag.

media.credit: Photo: Bjørn Christian Tørrissen, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: The statue of Christ the Redeemer looks out over which city?
questions.explanation: The statue stands on top of Corcovado mountain and was finished in 1931.

questions.question: Which famous building is this?
questions.explanation: The emperor Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

media.alt: A white marble building with a large dome
media.credit: Photo: Yann; edited by Jim Carter, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: In which city is this ancient building?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum could hold at least 50,000 people, who came to watch shows and games.

questions.question: The Golden Gate Bridge is in which American city?
questions.explanation: The bridge's colour is called International Orange, partly chosen so that it shows up in fog.

questions.question: How many presidents' faces are carved into Mount Rushmore?
questions.explanation: Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln each have a face about 18 metres tall.

questions.question: In which country is Machu Picchu, the ancient Inca city high in the mountains?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built in the 1400s, but the outside world only heard much about it in 1911.

questions.question: In which country is the Grand Canyon?
questions.explanation: The Colorado River took millions of years to carve out the Grand Canyon.

questions.question: In which city would you find the statue of the Little Mermaid?
questions.explanation: The statue is based on a fairy tale by the Danish writer Hans Christian Andersen.

questions.question: What are the giant stone statues on Easter Island called?
questions.explanation: The Rapa Nui people carved close to a thousand moai, mostly from the island's volcanic rock.

questions.question: Which is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing?
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid was the tallest building in the world for about 3,800 years.

questions.question: In which city is the giant skyscraper called the Burj Khalifa?
questions.explanation: The Burj Khalifa is about 828 metres tall, more than twice the height of London's Shard.

questions.question: In which city is the Sagrada Família, the church designed by Antoni Gaudí?
questions.explanation: Work on the Sagrada Família began way back in 1882.

questions.question: In which country is this castle?
questions.explanation: Neuschwanstein was built for King Ludwig II of Bavaria, and it inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

media.alt: A white castle on a wooded hillside
media.credit: Photo: Thomas Wolf, www.foto-tw.de, CC BY-SA 3.0 de (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: This stepped pyramid stands in which ancient city?
questions.explanation: At the spring and autumn equinoxes, shadows on El Castillo's steps look like a serpent sliding down.

media.credit: Photo: Daniel Schwen, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: In which city is this cathedral?
questions.explanation: St Basil's Cathedral was built on Red Square between 1555 and 1561 on the orders of Ivan the Terrible.

media.alt: A church with colourful onion domes

questions.question: The Parthenon in Athens was built as a temple to which goddess?
questions.explanation: The Parthenon stands on the Acropolis and was dedicated in 438 BC.

questions.question: In which city is the Hagia Sophia?
questions.explanation: Finished in 537, it was the largest cathedral in the world for nearly a thousand years.

questions.question: The Golden Temple, the holiest shrine of Sikhism, is in which Indian city?
questions.explanation: Its community kitchen serves free meals to tens of thousands of visitors every day.

questions.question: In the 1960s Egypt's giant temples at Abu Simbel were cut into blocks and moved uphill, to escape the lake made by which dam?
questions.explanation: The temples were rebuilt about 65 metres higher up, safe above the waters of Lake Nasser.

questions.question: In which city is the Brandenburg Gate?
questions.explanation: On top stands the Quadriga, a statue of a chariot pulled by four horses.

questions.question: Table Mountain looks down over which city?
questions.explanation: The layer of cloud that often covers its flat top is known as the 'tablecloth'.
